title.narrative: IFIT - Regional exchanges for peace, democracy and human rights
IFIT - Regionalt utbyte för fred, demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter

description.narrative:
The Latin America regional strategic framework for democracy and human rights of the Institution for Integrated Transitions (IFIT) aims to "bring about greater stability, inclusiveness, and respect for human rights and the rule of law in fragile and conflict-affected Latin American societies". To achieve this overarching goal, the project will leverage the potential of IFITs business model by engaging three key components:
1) in-country brain trust work: to ensure that local civil society actors participate and have influence in decision-making processes.
2) foster regional networking and peer exchanges on relevant experiences and lesson-sharing exchanges across Latin America through IFITs thematic practice groups.
3) provide an intervention logic for regional linkages to key global policy initiatives.
The combination of these three components will generate two specific outcomes that, together, will contribute to the projects overarching goal. These two outcomes are:
Outcome 1: Increased influence and engagement of local civil society actors in political processes and policymaking relating to human rights, democracy, and peacebuilding in conflict-affected societies.
Outcome 2: Policymakers develop better-informed policies and make greater use of key knowledge on the most relevant cross-cutting lessons from conflict and democratic transitions in Latin America. The framework will be supported by a high-level Regional Advisory Council.

Detta är ett projektstöd i linje med område 1 av Strategin för Sveriges Regionala Utvecklingssamarbete med Latin-Amerika, speciellt om mänskliga rättigheter och demokrati för IFIT (Institute for Integrated Transitions) som syftar till att skapa ökad stabilitet, integration samt respekt för mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstatsprincipen i bräckliga och konfliktdrabbade latinamerikanska samhällen. Den föreslagna insatsen kommer att dra nytta av potentialen i IFIT:s affärsmodell genom att använda tre nyckelkomponenter som utgör kärnan i dess verksamhet: 1) Stärka IFIT:s arbete för expertgrupper på plats samt deras förslag till lösningar när det gäller dynamiken, utmaningarna och möjligheterna beträffande demokrati, rättsstatsprincipen och mänskliga rättigheter i regionen. 2) Främja regionalt nätverkande och kollegialt utbyte av relevanta erfarenheter och lärdomar i Latinamerika. 3) Koppla det lokala och regionala arbetet till centrala globala politiska initiativ. Denna verksamhet kommer att stödjas av en regional rådgivande nämnd på hög nivå.

This is a project support aligned within the first area of the Strategy of Sweden in Latin America, especially on human rights and democracy for IFIT (Institute for Integrated Transitions) that aims to bring about greater stability, inclusiveness, and respect for human rights and the rule of law in fragile and conflict-affected Latin American societies. The proposed intervention will leverage the potential of IFIT’s business model by engaging three key components that are at the core of its actions: 1) strengthen IFIT’s in-country expert groups work and proposed solutions in relation to the dynamics, challenges, and opportunities of democracy, rule of law, and human rights within the region; 2) foster regional networking and peer exchanges on relevant experiences and lessons learned in Latin America; and 3) connecting the local and regional work to key global policy initiatives. These activities will be supported by a high-level Regional Advisory Council.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement IFIT - Sida Regional Latin America
Decision on Contribution IFIT - Sida Regional Latin America

description.narrative:
Main Achievements during the three years of the project 2022-2025:
Outcome 1: Increased influence and engagement of local civil society actors in political processes and policymaking relating to human rights, democracy, and peacebuilding in conflict-affected societies. Over the last three years, IFIT has ensured higher levels of influence and engagement of civil society actors in policymaking in the region. This was achieved by ensuring safe spaces for IFIT country brain trust members for planning, brainstorming and formulating ideas around key issues in Colombia, Mexico and Venezuela, as well as by continuously engaging with stakeholders and decision-makers in each of the three countries. Influence in policymaking was observable through the provision of expert advice, policy assessments, and recommendations to local and national decision makers. Some figures of the activities carried out during the whole activity period are found below:
Colombia: IFIT supported peacebuilding in Colombia through extensive engagement with local and national stakeholders, including field visits, policy dialogues, and expert consultations. Its work strengthened civil society participation, informed implementation of the 2016 Peace Agreement and the Total Peace policy, and contributed to improvements in security policies and transitional justice mechanisms. During 20242025, IFIT also expanded efforts to reduce polarization and launched new dialogue platforms to generate policy recommendations on peacebuilding, security, and governance challenges.
Through their Brain Trust for the Colombian Transition, IFIT carried out a series of activities, including 14 field visits (Urabá, Magdalena Medio, Guvaire, Tolima, Tumaco thrice, Ocaña, Pasto twice, Chocó twice, Bajo Cauca, Medellín), 51 Brain Trust meetings, six strategic retreats, and 220 meetings with local and national leaders, decision makers, and stakeholders.
Their work was encompassed within the following topics:
- Expert advice to support implementation of the 2016 Peace Agreement (transitional justice) - Local peacebuilding efforts and strategies to counter violence - Enhancing the Viability of the Total Peace Policy - Narratives and polarisation
Mexico:
Between 2022 and 2025, IFITs work in Mexico focused on improving policy discussions, supporting local efforts to address violence, and developing new approaches to tackling organised crime. Its activities centered on three areas: strengthening institutions and democratic governance, promoting local dialogue and peacebuilding responses, and exploring negotiation and mediation strategies for organised crime, including training for faith-based actors. To support these goals, IFIT and the Mexican Brain Trust organized 18 meetings, two strategic retreats, seven field visits across multiple states, and more than 50 engagements with government officials, academics, private sector representatives, civil society organizations, and international stakeholders.
Their work was encompassed within the following topics:
- Institutional reforms and democratic governance - Local dialogues and responses to violence and peace - Negotiation and mediation with criminal groups
Venezuela:
IFITs work in Venezuela has focused on creating conditions for a negotiated democratic transition and the restoration of democratic institutions. Its efforts centered on three main areas: providing technical support for negotiations and political agreements, developing policy frameworks for a future democratic transition, and engaging international stakeholders to maintain dialogue channels. These activities included 40 GEV meetings, six strategic retreats, 270 bilateral engagements with political and civil society leaders, four field visits, and 12 outreach missions to international actors influential in Venezuelas political landscape.
Their work was encompassed within the following topics:
- Technical support to negotiations and political agreements - Reflection and planning on Venezuelas democratic transition - Strategic engagement and facilitation with international actors
Regional work: During the reporting period, IFIT strengthened its Regional Programme for Latin America and the Caribbean by turning previously ad hoc knowledge-sharing initiatives into a structured platform for comparative analysis, regional dialogue, and cross-country collaboration. The programme connected lessons from Colombia, Mexico, and Venezuela with broader regional discussions, enabling national experiences to inform regional policy debates while enhancing country-level strategies through shared learning. This approach increased the impact of Swedens support by promoting the exchange of policy lessons and practical responses across the region. The programme focused on three key areas: integrating security issues into democratic governance discussions, facilitating regional dialogue on elections and institutional integrity, and strengthening SouthSouth learning networks.
Their work was encompassed within the following topics:
- Integrating security challenges into debates on democratic governance in Latin America - Regional policy dialogue on elections and institutional integrity - Network consolidation and SouthSouth exchange
Moreover, IFIT launched IFITe Cuenta, a podcast designed to make discussions on peacebuilding, security, violence, and transitional justice more accessible across Latin America and the Caribbean. The podcast has released 17 episodes featuring experts from multiple countries. Alongside its research, regional dialogues, and cross-country exchanges, this initiative has helped IFIT strengthen a regional platform for comparative learning and policy engagement, connecting national experiences to regional debates and generating practical, policy-relevant recommendations for decision-makers and practitioners.
Outcome 2: Policymakers develop better-informed policies and make greater use of key knowledge on the most relevant cross-cutting lessons from conflict and democratic transitions in Latin America.
IFITs Regional Programme for Latin America and the Caribbean is built around three interconnected pillars: regional analysis and knowledge generation, exchanges among experts, and capacity strengthening and advisory support for actors working in contexts of democratic fragility and violence. These elements create a continuous learning cycle in which regional dialogue identifies challenges, comparative research develops practical solutions, capacity-building activities support local implementation, and lessons from practice inform future research and policy engagement. This approach helps ensure that IFITs research and convening efforts translate into meaningful and sustainable policy and practice outcomes across the region.
Main activities at the regional level:
• Regional Advisory Council meetings: IFIT has consolidated the Regional Advisory Council for Latin America (CoAli) as a key strategic body guiding the development of the Regional Programme.
• Regional exchanges: IFIT organised 19 regional exchanges bringing together 217 experts and practitioners (116 women and 101 men) in several topics such as:
*Democratic governance and institutional design *Security governance and organised crime *Electoral dynamics and risks to democratic institutions *Geopolitical dynamics affecting the region
• Capacity-building workshops: IFIT conducted capacity-building workshops and peer-learning exchanges to strengthen the skills of civic actors and practitioners working in environments affected by violence, democratic fragility, and political repression. These initiatives transformed comparative research into practical tools and promoted SouthSouth learning by enabling participants facing similar governance challenges to share experiences and solutions. The topics comprised:
*Strengthening civic actors in restrictive environments *Institutional responses to violence and humanitarian crises *Electoral processes
• Country visits and regionally informed support to specific countries: These visits served two purposes: providing direct analytical support to countries facing acute governance or security challenges, and generating first-hand knowledge to inform IFITs broader regional analysis on democracy, security and institutional resilience. These meetings were focus:
* Provifing targeted analytical support and comparative reflections to actors in Ecuador and Haiti, two contexts facing significant governance and security challenges. *IFIT conducted visits to El Salvador and Guatemala aimed at strengthening our comparative analysis of key regional trends, particularly in the areas of security policy, democratic governance, and judicial independence.
• Regional Programmes contribution to IFITs global work: Insights and experiences from IFITs work in Latin America have played an important role in shaping the organizations global research, policy concepts, and learning processes. This influence has occurred mainly through the development of innovative research and policy ideas, as well as through the active participation of Latin American experts in IFITs global convenings and practitioner networks. This work was focus on:
* Contribution to research and innovative policy concepts * Participation of Latin American experts in IFITs global network and events
